what_it_does: For decades, computer systems researchers hand-crafted rules to make decisions — which job to run next on a server, how to route network traffic, when to flush data from memory. Machine learning (ML) offers an alternative: train models on historical data and let them make those decisions automatically. This paper asks a big-picture question: has ML-for-systems research reached an 'AlexNet moment' — the kind of breakthrough in 2012 that made ML the dominant approach to image recognition almost overnight? The authors survey ML adoption across many systems sub-fields (scheduling, compilers, storage, networking, etc.) and examine whether ML has truly displaced handcrafted approaches or is still one tool among many. It is a position paper offering analysis and perspective rather than new experimental results.
